etymologies.etymologyHTML: From operation +‎ -al.

definitions.definition: Of or relating to operations, especially military operations.

quote.citation: 2013 June 22, “Engineers of a different kind”, in The Economist, volume 407, number 8841, page 70:
quote.text: Private-equity nabobs bristle at being dubbed mere financiers. […] Much of their pleading is public-relations bluster. Clever financial ploys are what have made billionaires of the industry’s veterans. “Operational improvement” in a portfolio company has often meant little more than promising colossal bonuses to sitting chief executives if they meet ambitious growth targets. That model is still prevalent today.

quote.citation: 1977, George Lucas, Governor Tarkin, Star Wars:
quote.text: Princess Leia, before your execution, you will join me at a ceremony that will make this battle station operational. No star system will dare oppose the Emperor now.

quote.citation: 2022 December 14, “News in pictures: Class 87 soldiers on in Bulgaria”, in RAIL, number 972, page 26, photo caption:
quote.text: Despite somewhat faded paintwork, 87017 Iron Duke is clearly very much operational, as confirmed here on September 4.

definitions.definition: Determined by means of practical measures.
